728), (369, 730), (659, 732), (474, 734).

By hand. rho = 466 / (240.0e-6 m x 180.0e-6 m) = 1.0787e10 per m^2. For bending about [001] by edge dislocations of (110)[1-10] and (1-10)[110] in equal numbers, Nye: 1/R = rho (a/2), since each Burgers vector (a/2)<110> has the component a/2 = 0.20135 nm along [100]. 1/R = 1.0787e10 x 0.20135e-9 = 2.172 per m, R = 0.4604 m, i.e. 0.46 m. Counts 462 to 471 all give 0.46 m.

The most tempting wrong answer is 0.33 m, from 1/R = rho b with b = a/sqrt2. b = a gives 0.23 m; counting the flat-bottomed pits too gives 0.32 m.

A check in Python, standard library only:

a = 0.4027e-9
rho = 466/(240.0e-6*180.0e-6)
print(rho, 2/(rho*a))   # 1.0787e10, 0.4604

Sources: Nye, Acta Metall. 1, 153 (1953); Gilman and Johnston, J. Appl. Phys. 27, 1018 (1956); Johnston and Gilman, J. Appl. Phys. 30, 129 (1959); Ashby, Philos. Mag. 21, 399 (1970).
